10. Payment of all City bills when properly approved

11. Resolutions, Ordinances, etc.

   A. Approving that, in accordance with Section 23-22 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Middletown, the
      19 acres of open space located on three (3) parcels of property at Boston Road, identified as Assessor’s
      Map 14, Lot 0042, a portion of Assessor’s Map 14, Lot 0043, and Assessor’s Map 14, Lot 0182, be named
      the “Robert D. Cyranowicz Open Space.”

   B. Approving that the Mayor is authorized to sign and submit an application to the State of Connecticut for a
      grant in the amount of $36,750 in Local Capital Projects Improvement Program (LoCIP) funds, for the cost
      to repair critical elements of the Splash Pad; and that a new line item be created in the Capital Improvement
      Plan entitled “Splash Pad Repairs” in the amount of $36,750.

   C. Approving following distribution Health Department Opioid Settlement Funds: All-In Recovery -- $
      30,000.00; Community Health Center, Inc. -- $30,000.00; Community Renewal Team -- $20,000.00; Gilead
      -- $19,000.00; Governor’s Prevention Partnership -- $20,000.00; Rushford Center -- $25,000.00; St. Vincent
      DePaul -- $25,000.00; The Connection -- $6,000.00; TOTAL -- $175,000.00; and that any agency receiving
      an award must comply with the matching fund Code of Ordinances, Chapter 44, Section 44-11, section B,
      Municipal Grant Awards.
OCTOBER 5, 2026                      COMMON COUNCIL -- REGULAR MEETING                                       Page 4

    D. Approving the following distribution of Educational Incentive Challenge Grant funds: Oddfellows Playhouse
       -- After School Classes and Oddbridge -- $7,500; Cross Street Training & Academic Center, Inc. --
       Afterschool Tutorial Program -- $7,500; YMCA -- Kid’s Korner Before & After School -- $7,500; Ekklesia
       Contemporary Ballet -- Empowering Youth -- $7,500; TOTAL APPROPRIATION --              $30,000.00;    that
       citizens of Middletown are urged to ensure that every child has access to a safe, engaging place where
       students extend their learning day through enrichment and academic activities by supporting programming
       outside the school day; and that any agency receiving an award must comply with the matching fund Code
       of Ordinances, Chapter 44, Section 44-11, section B, Municipal Grant Awards.

    E. Approving a 5-year lease agreement, with an option for one (1) additional 5 year term, with the Razor to
       the Rosary LLC for 900 sq. ft. of rentable space at the R. M. Keating Historical Enterprise Park, 180 Johnson
       Street (“Keating Park”); and that the Mayor is hereby authorized to sign all documents necessary to
       implement the lease subject to review and approval by the office of General Counsel as to form and content.

    F. Approving the map, attached as Exhibit A, for attachment to the Memorandum of Agreement previously
       approved by Resolution No. 86-26; and that the Mayor is authorized to execute any documents necessary
       to attach the map to the Memorandum of Agreement, subject to review and approval as to form and content
       by the Office of General Counsel.

    G. Approving that Resolution No 146-25 is rescinded; and that any proposed lease of the premises may be
       submitted to the Common Council for consideration under a new resolution.

    H. Approving a 5-year lease agreement, with an option for one (1) additional 5-year term, with the Project Big
       Sky, LLC for 6,600 sq. ft. of rentable space at the R. M. Keating Historical Enterprise Park, 180 Johnson
       Street (“Keating Park”); and that the Mayor is hereby authorized to sign all documents necessary to
       implement the lease subject to review and approval by the office of General Counsel as to form and content.

    I.   Approving that the Mayor is authorized to cap the building permit fee at $100,000 for the Northern Middlesex
         YMCA’s estimated $22 million renovation and expansion project, excluding required state education fees,
         located at 99 Union Street.

         SUBSTITUTION: Approving that the Mayor to cap the building permit fees at $100,000.00 for the Northern
         Middlesex YMCA’s estimated $13.38 million in construction costs associated with their $22 million
         renovation and expansion project, excluding required state education fees, located at 99 Union Street.

    J.   Approving that the Triangle Community Center (TCC) is awarded the bid for RFP# 2026-019 Financial
         Agent for Middletown Pride; that the City may enter into a five (5) year agreement with Triangle Community
         Center for the engagement of Financial Agent services in the total amount of $345,091; that the Mayor
         and/or such other appropriate City officials are hereby authorized to execute any agreements and
         documents necessary to effectuate said agreement; and that said agreement shall be subject to review and
         approval as to form by the Office of General Counsel.

    K. Approving the 2026 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Entitlement appropriations, totaling
       $513,605; that the Mayor, as Chief Executive Officer of the City of Middletown, is authorized to submit a
       new 2026 Annual Action Plan to access $513,605 of CDBG entitlement funding, reprogramming of prior
       years’ unspent dollars and program income; and that a new Consolidated Plan may be approved to reflect
       Community Development Block Grant programs approved by the Common Council and changing priorities
       of present and future potential grant recipients.

12. Mayor’s Appointments
     Middletown Housing Authority

13. Adjournment
